title: FluidNC UART I/O expander
description: Describes a UART-attached I/O expander (e.g. Airedale, see wiki.fluidnc.com/en/hardware/official/airedale) in the same terms board.schema.json and module.schema.json use, so the wizard's role pickers, output_profile/common annotation, etc. work unchanged. Unlike a CNC I/O Module (plugs into a board's expansion socket; pins addressed by socket position and resolved to that board's mcu_pins), an expander connects over a UART link -- to a board's own expansion_uart connector, or to one provided by a module -- and each of its I/O is addressed by a fixed IO NUMBER (`io`) that FluidNC sees as the virtual pin uart_channel<N>.<io>. <N> is the uart number a config assigns to that link, a config-authoring fact decided at wizard runtime, never recorded here. One expander per uart channel; daisy-chaining is not modeled. Link parameters (baud/mode) are fixed by the expander's firmware protocol. The electrical vocabulary (input_profile, output_profile incl. drive_type and common) is board.schema.json's own, referenced rather than copied so it can't drift.

id.description: Lowercase snake_case identifier. Filename should be <id>.expander.yaml; a photo/hotspot file, if any, should be images/<id>_expander.jpg and hotspots/<id>_expander.hotspots.yaml -- the _expander suffix (like modules' _module) keeps ids from colliding with board/module ids in the shared images/ and hotspots/ directories.

min_fluidnc_version.description: Optional. Oldest FluidNC firmware that supports this expander's protocol (e.g. "3.9.6" for Airedale).

uart_link.description: The fixed UART parameters this expander's firmware protocol requires -- the wizard writes these into the uartN: block it generates for the link, same as it does for an expansion_uart connector's own baud/mode.

io.description: The expander firmware's own I/O number -- the <io> in uart_channel<N>.<io>. NOT an MCU pin number of whatever chip is inside the expander (the wiki is explicit that these are unrelated). Unique within a file.

label.description: The expander's OWN label for this I/O (silkscreen or vendor documentation term) -- purely positional/cosmetic.

generic_name.description: Normalized name, same convention as board.schema.json's generic_pin.generic_name ("In<io>", "5V Out<io>", "FET<io>", ...) with <io> in place of <pin>. Needs to be unique only within this expander (hotspot files for an expander are keyed against this file alone). Optional -- tools fall back to label.

direction.description: Fixed per I/O by the expander firmware's own capability table -- unlike a board's generic_pin there is no 'either' or 'bidirectional' here (an I/O that is genuinely switchable can be listed once per use, as boards do, if one ever exists).

pwm_timer.description: Present only on an output that can do PWM, and names the expander's hardware timer that generates it. Per-pin, NOT a bus-level fact (contrast board.schema.json's BUS_PWM_CAPABLE for gpio/i2so): the same expander has PWM-capable and plain outputs. Pins sharing a pwm_timer must be configured for the same PWM frequency -- the firmware alarms otherwise -- and the expander has a limited number of distinct timers (Airedale: 4), so this is what lets a tool warn about conflicts. Omit on inputs and on non-PWM outputs.
